approach.method_basis: The reference is RACOS, introduced by Yu, Qian and Hu in their 2016 paper, Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification. It uses observed objective values to label promising examples as positive and poorer examples as negative. In its categorical form, it selects a positive exemplar and randomly fixes coordinates to that exemplar's values until every observed negative example lies outside the remaining region. It then fixes more coordinates as needed to limit how many remain free. New proposals sample the free coordinates uniformly while preserving the fixed values. A broader uniform sampling component maintains exploration, and fresh randomized classifiers can define different regions around the same exemplar. Feedback updates the examples that guide subsequent regions.
approach.novelty: This root applies categorical RACOS directly to molecular SELFIES token frames, using removable padding to permit length changes and a construction alphabet extracted from the unlabeled corpus. Initial molecules enter classification only after a verified molecular identity round trip. Each accepted generated molecule retains its actual sampled frame and returned score, with one record per canonical molecule. Ranked labels include all ties at the positive cutoff and stay fixed throughout each announced batch. Decoding, chemical validation and novelty filtering connect raw frame sampling to oracle submissions; exhausted regions trigger reconstruction or the declared broad sampling component. The implementation also compares each final region with the same-coordinate-order restriction from the free-coordinate limit alone, so any additional restriction caused by negatives is visible. These choices test whether exact exclusion in token coordinates produces useful molecular proposals while keeping representation identity, decoded duplication and the contribution of negative examples separately measurable.

observed_bottleneck: This root has no Parent or evaluated RACOS node. Its difficulty is converting a small set of real molecular scores into useful categorical construction constraints when positional token similarity may poorly reflect molecular improvement. The confirmed nodes n-9bd1200edbf6 and n-bd0cbfe35fa3 each report only 6/480 exact canonical reconstructions from their learned VAE, despite lower heldout reconstruction loss and correct generated-position score joins. The refuted n-77c41c9bc036 instead concerns a stricter token-inversion failure after flow adaptation. Direct verified SELFIES frames remove those learned-inverse prerequisites; none of that evidence establishes useful RACOS exclusion regions or a serialization-order bottleneck. The supplied cluster history is empty.
hypothesis: Rank real task-local molecular observations into positive and negative examples, build fresh categorical regions by randomly fixing a positive exemplar's SELFIES-frame coordinates until every observed negative frame is excluded and the remaining free-coordinate count is bounded, then sample uniform token assignments inside those regions with a broader uniform construction-space component.

finding_summary.headline: RACOS ran correctly; negative exclusion added no restrictions beyond the uncertainty limit
finding_summary.insights:
Negative examples were consulted and newly admitted negatives prolonged the exclusion phase in 330 regions, so the classifier was active. Yet exclusion always finished after at most 70 fixed coordinates, while the uncertainty limit required 75. The limit therefore determined every final mask, and perfect exclusion supplies no evidence for an additional contribution of negative labels to proposal geometry or score. The observed procedure supports direct molecular score provenance and feedback-guided sampling around positively ranked exemplars; whether making negatives influence the final region improves search remains open.

Distinct token restrictions also did not imply distinct molecular neighborhoods: 48 raw decodes overlapped an earlier different region, and ten draws recovered a currently negative molecular identity through another encoding. Filtering caught these cases, but it cannot repair weak molecular geometry. The molecular assessment finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive linkages among high scorers, with only an uneven subset of conventional scaffold chemistry. Together with the low exemplar-beating rate and the unchanged median_2 incumbent, this identifies useful, chemically credible token neighborhoods as an unresolved bottleneck. Neither reliable performance across seeds nor a benefit from alternative serialization views is established.
finding_summary.results:
All five objectives completed on the screening seed, with 300 evaluations each and all 1,450 generated submissions accepted. Every initial molecule preserved its identity through token encoding, every returned score stayed attached to its actual sampled frame, and all 150 rank-label snapshots included the required cutoff ties. All 1,355 constructed regions retained their positive exemplar and reduced the number of included observed negatives to zero, while leaving exactly four of 79 token positions free. Real feedback was reused: all 1,400 generated observations with a later opportunity participated in subsequent region construction. However, the final restrictions in every region were identical to those obtained from the four-free-coordinate limit alone.

The five-task final Top-1 mean was 0.315539, compared with 0.208492 for the supplied initial observations. Initial-to-final Top-1 scores were 0.305105 to 0.345581 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.548381 to 0.579123 for deco_hop, 0.019041 to 0.120104 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.167839 for median_2, and 0.002094 to 0.365051 for sitagliptin_mpo. All 18 incumbent improvements came from regional submissions. Only 67 of 1,304 accepted regional proposals (5.14%) beat their selected exemplar; mean child-minus-exemplar score was -0.096376. There is no Parent comparison or additional seed in this root experiment, so these within-run gains do not establish a comparative score advantage.

molecular.headline: Frequent rings, but high scorers often carry radicals, unusual charges and reactive linkages; conventional scaffold chemistry is uneven.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied seed-0 trajectories were read, each containing 300 observations and 290 optimizer proposals. There is no Parent node or Parent trajectory, so comparisons use the supplied initial molecules and the within-task score contrasts. The output ranges from tiny heteroatom fragments to medium and larger multiring frameworks. Rings are common: the per-task ring_closure_rate spans 0.6241 to 0.8207. Aromatic content is uneven, with aromatic_atom_rate spanning 0.1517 to 0.6207; those rates describe the presence of SMILES text features, not fractions of atoms or perceived aromatic rings. Some recognizable neutral indole carboxamides, aryl aminals and fused nitrogen/carbonyl frameworks survive. However, charged_rate spans 0.6862 to 0.9448, and reparsing the supplied trajectory graphs confirms widespread radical centres as well as formal charges. Oxonium-containing unsaturated rings, low-coordinate charged atoms, atypical sulfur/phosphorus environments, peroxides and highly unsaturated chains recur among the high scorers. The ring and aromaticity judgements therefore reflect real but inconsistent coverage; they do not imply chemically credible ring geometry. Formal atom and bond diversity is substantial, while high-scoring chemistry within a task repeatedly returns to related scaffold families. Synthetic plausibility is poor overall, with a more conventional subset particularly visible in the aryl-aminal and fused-dicarbonyl families. Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0, which establishes absent stereochemical specification rather than absence of potentially stereogenic structures. The score observations establish local structural associations. They do not identify an unseen target pharmacophore or show that a chemically cleaner analogue would necessarily score better.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized unsaturated organic frameworks, interspersed with very small fragments; mean SMILES length is 42.1 and maximum length 84. The ring_closure_rate is 0.8207 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6207. The high-scoring proposals combine benzene or other aromatic fragments with nitrogen-rich thione/thioamide linkages, N-N or N=N connectivity, and oxygen-containing unsaturated rings. Evaluation 135 adds an exocyclic boron double bond, oxonium and a low-coordinate carbon cation to a densely connected multiring framework. Evaluation 21 retains aryl thiourea-like connectivity but embeds an alkyne in an oxonium-containing ring system. These are substantially less convincing synthetic targets than the supplied neutral methoxyindole carboxamide at evaluation 9. The generated set has charged_rate 0.9241 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.2069.
liabilities: Persistent oxonium centres, a radical-bearing low-coordinate carbon cation in evaluation 135, and additional radical nitrogen/oxygen environments elsewhere in the digest.
Cyclic alkynes, cumulated unsaturation, exocyclic boron double bonds and unusually connected N-N/thione systems make stability and feasible synthesis doubtful.
missing_features: Reliable preservation and variation of compact aromatic frameworks with intact nitrogen/carbonyl or nitrogen/thione linkages; these features coexist in the stronger supplied examples but are frequently disrupted in the lower-scoring generated structures.

Chemically ordinary, closed-shell versions of the high-scoring aromatic/polar architectures. The initial neutral indole carboxamide demonstrates relevant coverage, but the leading proposals largely explore oxonium-rich alternatives; the data do not establish a score benefit from neutrality itself.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 135 scores 0.3455806835841063, evaluation 21 scores 0.3430778750697882, and the aryl/N=N/thioamide-containing evaluation 195 scores 0.34169169616841205. The neutral initial indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 already scores 0.3051048083696145, whereas the initial aryl-rich nitrogen/thione compound at evaluation 3 scores 0.1501184006136499. The tiny imidate-like anion at evaluation 289 scores 0.0. In the final excerpt, evaluation 295 retains an unsaturated oxonium ring but replaces the thione/aromatic arrangement with a thiol-bearing branched chain and scores 0.07284283327394388. The visible preference is for particular assembled aromatic/nitrogen-containing frameworks and their linker arrangements over fragments or damaged arrangements. Neither aromatic ring presence alone nor an unusual charge establishes a favourable contribution.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-sized aryl-rich molecules and smaller chain fragments; mean SMILES length is 41.9 and maximum length 85. The ring_closure_rate is 0.7724 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.5655. The upper tail includes methoxyindole carboxamide/amidine derivatives with a fluoropyridyl group, and linked diaryl cyclic aminals carrying methoxy, fluoroethoxy, methyl and sometimes hydroxyl groups. The neutral cyclic-aminal members at evaluations 138 and 253 have recognizable organic functionality, although ring construction and hydroxyaminal stability remain unestablished. Other close members replace ordinary substituents with peroxide/alkoxide chains, an aryl-bound nitrogen anion or an O-Cl group. The full proposal set has charged_rate 0.6862 and halogen_rate 0.6828.
liabilities: Peroxide bonds combined with terminal alkoxide groups in the highest-scoring indole series, and reactive O-Cl functionality in a high-scoring aminal analogue.

The aryl-bound nitrogen anion in evaluation 296 is a deprotonated amine environment, not a conventional neutral amine. Hydroxylated aminal centres and complex cyclizations also warrant caution even in otherwise neutral members.
missing_features: Broader stable substitution chemistry around the retained aryl/nitrogen frameworks. Near-leading neutral examples are present, but other leading decorations introduce chemically labile bonds or strongly basic anions without demonstrating that those features are necessary.

Additional coherent scaffold families that preserve the aromatic and polar-group relationships visible in the stronger molecules; the high-scoring excerpt mainly recycles indole and diaryl-aminal arrangements. Exact hidden decoration requirements cannot be inferred from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The indole amidine with a peroxide-containing alkoxide substituent at evaluation 272 scores 0.5791225581141548; its corresponding carboxamide at evaluation 187 scores 0.5711425931629196. This pair supports a local preference for the amidine change within that particular scaffold. The neutral diaryl hydroxyaminal at evaluation 138 scores 0.5766980825479363, exactly the score of the related O-Cl-containing evaluation 205. The aryl nitrogen anion at evaluation 296 scores 0.5782514840798705, while the neutral gem-dimethyl aminal at evaluation 253 scores 0.5749037932930181. Tiny formaldehyde at evaluation 244 and the short chlorinated ether at evaluation 270 both score 0.5. The final, partly de-aromatized evaluation 299 scores 0.5387550321456468. The observed gradient favours coherent multiaryl nitrogen-containing architecture over small fragments, with modest changes among the high-scoring substituent variants; it does not show that peroxide, O-Cl or anionic functionality is required.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail consists of relatively large, densely connected polycyclic frameworks with chlorinated and fluorinated aryl regions, unsaturated bridges, and sulfur/nitrogen-rich linkages. Mean SMILES length is 57.7 and maximum length 108. The ring_closure_rate is 0.7, but aromatic_atom_rate is only 0.2586: the many rings and double bonds across the trajectory do not generally correspond to intact aromatic systems. The best examples recover aromatic regions within heavily modified scaffolds. Evaluations 213, 273 and 260 contain small-ring nitrilium/triple-bond segments, unusual sulfur environments and radical centres. Cationic nitrogen can also carry covalently bound chlorine. These are poor candidates for straightforward synthesis despite being parseable graphs. The proposal set has charged_rate 0.9034 and halogen_rate 0.8552.
liabilities: Small-ring triple-bond/nitrilium geometry, radical nitrogen centres and covalent N-Cl functionality in the leading polycycles.

Atypical sulfur/phosphorus coordination, extensive halogenation and unresolved stereochemical/conformational possibilities make the apparent rigid frameworks chemically doubtful. No binding poses or experimental stability evidence are supplied.
missing_features: Chemically credible realization of the combined aryl surface, constrained shape and polar/ionizable functionality represented in the upper tail. The leading molecules express much of their nitrogen chemistry through nitrilium or low-coordinate charged/radical environments.

Well-defined saturated nitrogen heterocycles and specified stereochemistry within otherwise intact aryl frameworks are poorly represented among the leading generated examples. This is a chemistry-coverage gap; the low score of the initial tertiary-amine molecule prevents claiming that a particular amine centre would solve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The elaborate halogenated polycycle at evaluation 213 scores 0.12010438063540518, the phosphorus-containing relative at evaluation 273 scores 0.118818265142154, and the boron/ammonium-containing evaluation 260 scores 0.11451910258577357. The initial conventional aryl/sulfonamide/carboxamide framework at evaluation 10 scores 0.01904115112334333. A short neutral ether/formamide at evaluation 86 scores 0.001217586292651792. The initial aromatic hydroxamate/amide bearing a saturated tertiary amine at evaluation 6 scores still lower, 0.0003786988088202195, so a basic amine plus aromatic rings is not sufficient in the supplied observations. The truncated final charged sulfur/nitrogen structure at evaluation 296 scores 0.007096085062148271. The visible preference is associated with the fuller halogenated, conformationally constrained, heteroatom-bearing architecture. These examples do not isolate a causal benefit from charge, radical character or any specific binding interaction.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger proposals are medium-to-large, aromatic and carbonyl-rich frameworks related to the initial phenolic aryl ethyl ester linked to an N-methylated fused dicarbonyl heterocycle and a phenyl group. Mean SMILES length is 48.6 and maximum length 87; ring_closure_rate is 0.7966 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.5276. Evaluation 252 makes a further methylene-linked annulation while retaining ordinary ester, phenol and cyclic carbonyl functionality. Evaluation 144 retains the fused dicarbonyl portion but has a nonaromatic cyclopentadienone region. These neutral examples are more synthetically recognizable than the boron/sulfur ring insertion at evaluation 161 or the many charged and partly opened variants elsewhere. The full generated set still has charged_rate 0.7483 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1448; synthetic plausibility is mixed and scaffold-dependent.
liabilities: Boron/sulfur and phosphorus insertions, charged substitutions and partial destruction of aromatic or cyclic carbonyl systems throughout the generated set.

The most conventional generated annulation still creates a more demanding fused architecture, while cyclopentadienone and cumulated-unsaturation variants raise reactivity and geometric concerns. Parseability does not supply a synthetic route.
missing_features: Controlled, chemically ordinary variation that retains the combined aromatic/ester/carbonyl topology while changing its arrangement; the strongest generated examples remain close to an initially supplied family.

Broader coverage of distinct intact aromatic amide-rich scaffolds alongside the dominant fused-dicarbonyl series. The separate initial amide/hydroxamate is also relatively strong, but it is absent from the best-generated digest excerpt; no unseen reference structure can be deduced from that contrast.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl ester/fused dicarbonyl compound at evaluation 7 remains the observed maximum at 0.1678386594791329. The strongest generated annulated relative at evaluation 252 scores 0.16526725762745997, the boron/sulfur-containing relative at evaluation 161 scores 0.16482878931282252, and evaluation 144 scores 0.15842507656543134. The chemically distinct initial aromatic amide/hydroxamate at evaluation 6 also scores 0.1569767171139282. At the end, the short ether/aldehyde at evaluation 299 scores 0.031008683647302127, and the tiny boron/phosphorus/silicon/iodine fragment at evaluation 300 scores 0.0. Retention of assembled aromatic and carbonyl-containing motifs is associated with higher scores than fragmentary chemistry. Extra annulation or unusual element insertion does not improve on the supplied initial maximum in these observations.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring output is predominantly nonaromatic: medium-sized branched polyenes, imine/azine chains and cumulated C=C=N-type linkages, with fluorinated termini and thiol-containing ether or silicon appendages. Some members have a small unsaturated nitrogen/boron or nitrogen/oxygen ring; the high-scoring evaluation 177 is acyclic. Mean SMILES length is 45.3 and maximum length 84. The overall ring_closure_rate is 0.6241, but aromatic_atom_rate is only 0.1517, cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.531 and charged_rate 0.9448. Evaluations 277, 177, 147 and 210 contain low-coordinate charged/radical nitrogen, phosphorus, boron or silicon environments. Their chemical identities are much closer to highly reactive heteroatom-rich unsaturated graphs than conventional isolable medicinal compounds.
liabilities: Multiple radical or low-coordinate charged centres within individual structures, including silicon and phosphorus environments that are unlike ordinary saturated silanes or phosphate/phosphonate groups.

Cumulated unsaturation, N-O bonds, long imine/azine or polyene sequences, thiol termini and unspecified stereochemistry give substantial stability and synthesis concerns. The upper scores do not establish medicinal plausibility.
missing_features: Chemically credible, closed-shell alternatives spanning the medium-sized mixed-heteroatom chain/ring arrangements sampled in the stronger molecules; the demonstrated high-score region is populated by radical-rich structures.

Stable, well-specified versions of the observed polar and unsaturated frameworks, with conventional ionization and stereochemical definition. Their score effect remains unmeasured; absent aromatic rings cannot honestly be called a score-supported deficiency here.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 277 scores 0.36505100258606615; the acyclic polyene/azine at evaluation 177 scores 0.3436199762843053. The boron-ring/silicon relative at evaluation 147 scores 0.3354265133232108 and its oxygen-ring relative at evaluation 210 scores 0.3251031345422294. Thus neither aromaticity nor ring closure is necessary for the high-score family visible here. The conventional initial aromatic ester/dicarbonyl compound at evaluation 7 scores only 0.0020944534688323298. The final modified relative at evaluation 296 scores 6.214769695340417e-08, and the truncated nitrile-containing chain at evaluation 298 scores 4.7513256368956235e-07. A heteroatom-dense charged chain at evaluation 300 scores 0.0. The gradient is sensitive to the assembled chain/ring and heteroatom arrangement; neither mere complexity nor charge density explains it. The observed median is 0.000102. The trajectory supplies no basis for prescribing a missing aromatic pharmacophore or a drug-specific amine pattern.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the supplied proposal sets, charged_rate ranges from 0.6862 to 0.9448. Reading and reparsing the same graphs reveals low-coordinate carbon/nitrogen radical centres and unusual radical-bearing silicon/phosphorus environments, including in upper-tail molecules. The charges are frequently oxonium, nitrilium, strongly basic anions or other atypical states rather than ordinary protonatable amines and carboxylates. The neutral indole carboxamide, neutral aryl aminal and neutral fused-dicarbonyl examples show that conventional electronic structures are also present in chemically relevant score regions.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably produce chemically credible electronic states while varying polar and ionizable functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make closed-shell polar structures and controlled, chemically credible ionization states routinely accessible. Construction constraints should distinguish ordinary ionic functional groups from unsupported radicals and low-coordinate charged atoms, while feedback determines which polar architectures matter. Element identity or a net-charge ban alone would not capture this gap.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The upper-tail indole series contains peroxide/alkoxide substituents. A neutral methoxy/fluoroethoxy aryl hydroxyaminal and an O-Cl-containing relative both score 0.5766980825479363. Other high-scoring examples contain cyclic alkynes, cumulated bonds or unusually connected sulfur groups. These liabilities are not resolved by successful parsing or by removing formal charge, and the score contrasts do not demonstrate that reactive decorations are necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent functional-group stability even when its proposed graph is neutral and closed-shell.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand ordinary stable ether, amide, amine and related substitution chemistry around the frameworks supported by current feedback. Chemical construction should account for labile bond combinations and ring strain as well as valence, allowing stable alternatives to be explored without encoding a particular objective or target structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stronger aromatic families retain assembled nitrogen/thione, aryl-aminal or fused-dicarbonyl patterns, while the low-scoring excerpts repeatedly contain small fragments or opened/de-aromatized versions. An initial intact aromatic ester/dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.1678386594791329; its strongest generated annulated relative scores 0.16526725762745997, whereas a late short ether/aldehyde scores 0.031008683647302127. The high-score nonaromatic family also loses score after substantial changes to its assembled heteroatom chain. Frequent ring closures therefore do not establish reliable preservation of useful topology.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot consistently vary useful scaffolds without disrupting aromatic rings and the linker or carbonyl groups that organize them.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support scaffold-preserving changes to substituents and attachment relationships while retaining explicit ring edges and complete functional-group bond patterns. Let the observed feedback identify which structures to preserve, and keep alternative coherent scaffolds accessible so preservation does not become fixation on an initial molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring_closure_rate spans 0.6241 to 0.8207, yet leading examples include highly unsaturated oxonium loops, small-ring nitrilium segments and complex heteroatom-rich bridges. Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. Saturated amine-containing rings are visible in supplied initial molecules, but the leading generated cationic ring examples often express charge through more problematic bonding. This establishes a coverage gap, not a measured preference for saturation or stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional saturated and stereochemically specified ring architectures are poorly covered among the stronger generated structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make feasible saturated and partly saturated heterocycles, controlled basic centres and explicitly specified stereochemical variants available as general construction options. Ring geometry and stereochemical identity should remain coherent during variation, with task-local feedback deciding where these chemical dimensions help.

method_name: RACOS: negative-exclusion sampling of de novo SELFIES regions
method_thesis: The anchor is RACOS, selected before locating the primary source. Its categorical form chooses a positively labeled exemplar, randomly fixes coordinates to that exemplar until negative examples are excluded, further restricts the number of free coordinates, and samples the resulting region; a broader uniform component preserves exploration. Each proposal can use a newly randomized classifier. These are the mechanisms described by Yu, Qian and Hu in [Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/10289/10148). My molecular adaptation applies this process directly to bounded categorical SELFIES frames, with removable padding that permits changes in molecular length. Preparation extracts only a construction-token alphabet from the permitted unlabeled corpus. There is no trained molecular encoder or decoder. Initial labeled molecules become exemplars only after encoding and decoding reproduce their canonical identity. For generated molecules, retain the actual sampled frame, its decoded canonical molecule, and the score actually returned for that molecule. Rank the current objective's observed molecules into a high-score positive group and a lower-score negative group; use these labels to construct exclusion regions. Free token positions are newly sampled and decoded into complete molecules, checked, canonicalized, and deduplicated. Rebuild a region or use the broad generation component when a region cannot provide a fresh molecule. These are online constructions from token primitives, not retrieval or enumeration of complete molecules. After each announced batch receives real feedback, refresh the labeled sets and incumbent; all pending proposals use only previously observed scores. Each objective starts with clean task-specific state and follows the protocol's supplied batch and resource limits. The hypothesis is that explicitly excluding observed poor token configurations will concentrate new molecular proposals around combinations that improve the incumbent with few labels. Success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Region exclusion, validity, or classification accuracy alone cannot establish that hypothesis. Positional token restrictions may have weak structural meaning, and multiple frames can decode to the same molecule; exact representation checks address score provenance but do not establish useful search geometry.
